encounters.cc: Generalized tonic-clonic seizure with posterior right shoulder dislocation

lines: Generalized tonic-clonic seizure with posterior right shoulder dislocation
A 32-year-old male is brought to the emergency department after experiencing a generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home.
His wife reports that he has a history of epilepsy and has been non-compliant with his medication regimen.
The patient is postictal and unable to provide a coherent history.
- HIV/AIDS (diagnosed age 27, AIDS-defining illness, intermittent adherence to antiretroviral therapy)
- Inflammatory bowel disease (indeterminate colitis with features of both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder (heroin)
- Colonoscopy with biopsy (age 28, diagnostic for IBD)
- Closed reduction of posterior right shoulder dislocation (age 32, secondary to seizure)
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day.
On examination, the patient's right arm is held in adduction and internal rotation, and there is a noticeable flattening of the anterior aspect of the shoulder.
He winces in pain when an attempt is made to externally rotate the shoulder.
An X-ray of the right shoulder is obtained and shows the humeral head internally rotated and positioned posterior to the glenoid.

lines: Persistent perioral rash, taste disturbance, and hair loss with chronic diarrhea

He admits to not adhering to his prescribed vitamin and mineral supplements.

encounters.cc: Worsening abdominal pain, distension, and bloody diarrhea

lines: Worsening abdominal pain, distension, and bloody diarrhea
This 34-year-old male with indeterminate colitis and HIV/AIDS was previously evaluated in Gastroenterology clinic for chronic diarrhea and zinc deficiency.
He presents to the emergency department with a two-day history of worsening abdominal pain, distension, and bloody diarrhea.
He reports having six to eight bloody bowel movements per day.
He has not been compliant with his mesalamine therapy.
- HIV/AIDS (diagnosed age 27, AIDS-defining illness, intermittent adherence to antiretroviral therapy)
- Inflammatory bowel disease (indeterminate colitis with features of both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder (heroin)
- Colonoscopy with biopsy (age 28, diagnostic for IBD)
- Closed reduction of posterior right shoulder dislocation (age 32, secondary to seizure)
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day.
On examination, his temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), heart rate is 120 bpm, and blood pressure is 95/60 mmHg.
His abdomen is distended, with tenderness to palpation diffusely, but no rebound or guarding.
An abdominal x-ray shows colonic dilation with a transverse colon diameter of 7 cm.

lines: Progressive headaches, nausea, confusion, and diplopia

On examination, the patient appears lethargic.
Neurological examination reveals bilateral lateral gaze palsy.

encounters.cc: Four-day history of fever, chills, productive cough with hemoptysis, and pleuritic chest pain

lines: Four-day history of fever, chills, productive cough with hemoptysis, and pleuritic chest pain

This 37-year-old male with HIV/AIDS complicated by prior opportunistic infections including cryptococcal meningitis and cerebral toxoplasmosis in the setting of intermittent antiretroviral therapy adherence reports that his sputum is thick, yellow, and occasionally streaked with blood.
He also endorses left-sided chest pain that worsens with deep breaths and coughing, as well as mild shortness of breath during exertion.
He has had similar symptoms once before, about a year ago, when he was hospitalized and treated for “a lung infection” with antibiotics and improved within a week.
- Toxic megacolon secondary to Clostridioides difficile infection (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
- HIV/AIDS (diagnosed age 27, AIDS-defining illness, intermittent adherence to antiretroviral therapy)
- Inflammatory bowel disease (indeterminate colitis with features of both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder (heroin)
He was diagnosed with HIV 4 years ago but was not engaged in regular medical care until recently.
His most recent CD4+ count was 110/µL.
- Colonoscopy with biopsy (age 28, diagnostic for IBD)
- Closed reduction of posterior right shoulder dislocation (age 32, secondary to seizure)
He began antiretroviral therapy 3 months ago and has been taking his medications consistently since then.
He smokes one pack of cigarettes daily and drinks alcohol socially.
He works as a food delivery driver and recently returned to work after recovering from a respiratory illness 5 weeks ago.
He lives alone and has not traveled recently.
He denies orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, leg swelling, or weight loss.
Temperature is 39.5°C (103.1°F), blood pressure is 118/62 mm Hg, pulse is 108/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air.
On examination, he appears fatigued and slightly diaphoretic but is alert and oriented.
Pulmonary examination reveals decreased breath sounds, dullness to percussion, and coarse crackles at the left lower lung field.
The remainder of the exam is unremarkable.
There is no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly.
Chest x-ray reveals a dense left lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms and no cavitation or effusion.

encounters.cc: Four days of worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, fever, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain

lines: Four days of worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, fever, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain

This 38-year-old male with HIV/AIDS with intermittent antiretroviral therapy adherence, history of cryptococcal meningitis, cerebral toxoplasmosis, and prior pneumococcal pneumonia one year prior, presents with 4 days of worsening shortness of breath, non-bloody productive cough, fever, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain.
He reports generalized fatigue, decreased appetite, and chills.
He has not seen a physician since his last hospitalization 12 months ago.
- Toxic megacolon secondary to Clostridioides difficile infection (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
- HIV/AIDS (diagnosed age 27, AIDS-defining illness, intermittent adherence to antiretroviral therapy)
- Inflammatory bowel disease (indeterminate colitis with features of both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder (heroin)
His past medical history is notable for HIV, diagnosed 6 years ago, but he has been off antiretroviral therapy for over 3 years.
- Colonoscopy with biopsy (age 28, diagnostic for IBD)
- Closed reduction of posterior right shoulder dislocation (age 32, secondary to seizure)
He lives alone and denies any recent travel, occupational exposures, or sick contacts.
He smokes a pack of cigarettes daily and occasionally uses intranasal cocaine.
Temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), blood pressure is 108/62 mmHg, heart rate is 112/min, respiratory rate is 26/min, and oxygen saturation is 93% on room air.
On examination, the patient is ill-appearing and mildly diaphoretic.
Pulmonary exam reveals dullness to percussion, decreased breath sounds, and crackles over the right posterior lung field.
There are no oral lesions or skin rashes.
Laboratory studies show a WBC count of 13,800/mm³ and a CD4 count of 72/µL.
A chest X-ray is obtained and shown below.

encounters.cc: Altered mental status concerning for heroin overdose

lines: Altered mental status concerning for heroin overdose

The 38-year-old male with a complex history of HIV/AIDS with intermittent antiretroviral adherence, prior opportunistic infections including cryptococcal meningitis and cerebral toxoplasmosis, and recurrent pneumococcal pneumonia most recently one month ago, presents with altered mental status.
The patient has a known history of intravenous drug use and is accompanied by friends who report heroin use with concern for overdose.
They further note that he was recently released from jail and has not been taking any prescribed medications.
Naloxone is administered with improvement in his respiratory rate and mental status.
However, the patient becomes agitated and refuses further treatment, attempting to leave the emergency department.
- Toxic megacolon secondary to Clostridioides difficile infection (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
- HIV/AIDS (diagnosed age 27, AIDS-defining illness, intermittent adherence to antiretroviral therapy)
- Inflammatory bowel disease (indeterminate colitis with features of both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder (heroin)
- Colonoscopy with biopsy (age 28, diagnostic for IBD)
- Closed reduction of posterior right shoulder dislocation (age 32, secondary to seizure)
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day.
Respiratory rate is 6 breaths per minute, heart rate is 55 beats per minute, blood pressure is 90/50 mmHg, and temperature is 36.6°C (97.9°F).
The patient's oxygen saturation is 89% on room air.
On examination, the patient is unresponsive to verbal commands.
His pupils are pinpoint, and there are track marks on his arms.
A fingerstick glucose level is 110 mg/dL.
